items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide security clearance, blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, and conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or results; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps are unavailable; authentication boundaries, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness are unverified. TLS evidence only shows no certificates expiring within 30 days and does not establish complete TLS posture. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 16 fail, and 6 unknown. Risk severity is high for public launch and medium for bounded changes that add no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Exact decision: retain private launch gates and permit only existing bounded read-only evidence work; do not claim certification or clean health.

Continue only the existing read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts. Record dated, redacted evidence or explicit unknowns for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Do not access credentials or private containers, change permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue, exploit targets, or conduct outreach.

Security-sensitive releases and public exposure remain blocked until material control evidence is available. Required evidence includes access boundaries, secret-handling controls, runtime isolation, release approvals and rollback, dependency provenance, TLS posture, data exposure, monitoring and incident response, and disclosure readiness. Do not treat unavailable fleet-doctor or operations results as evidence of safety.
